name: Astaxanthin
lead: Astaxanthin is a red keto-carotenoid pigment produced by the freshwater microalga Haematococcus pluvialis, the yeast Xanthophyllomyces dendrorhous and the bacterium Paracoccus carotinifaciens, and it is responsible for the pink-red colour of salmon, shrimp, krill and flamingos [1]. It is sold as a dietary supplement and, in synthetic form, is widely used as a feed colourant in aquaculture [1].

In appearance and skincare communities it is taken for skin hydration, elasticity and protection from UV-induced skin deterioration [3][5][4]. A 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials found that oral astaxanthin significantly improved moisture and elasticity compared with placebo but did not significantly reduce wrinkle depth [3]. Trials are mostly small and short.

It is regarded as generally recognized as safe in the United States for algae, synthetic and bacterial sources, and the EFSA set an acceptable daily intake of 0.2 mg per kg body weight in 2019 [1]. On T Nation it is mentioned mainly as an anti-inflammatory supplement [16][18][19].

paras: Oral astaxanthin is taken for skin moisture, elasticity and sun-related skin changes [3][4][6]. Community members stack it with other supplements for general skin and anti-inflammatory goals [16][18][17].

Astaxanthin is used in animal, aquaculture and human supplements, and as a feed additive to colour farmed salmon and egg yolks; synthetic carotenoid pigments account for 15 to 25 percent of the cost of production of commercial salmon feed [1]. Human trials have also examined eye strain in children, reproductive outcomes in endometriosis and PCOS, and oxidative stress [8][9][10][11].

Skin ageing: a 2021 systematic review and meta-analysis identified eleven studies: nine randomized controlled studies of oral astaxanthin and two open-label prospective studies of topical or oral-topical use. Oral supplementation improved moisture content (standardised mean difference 0.53) and elasticity (0.77), but did not significantly decrease wrinkle depth (-0.26, not significant) compared to placebo [3]. A separate 2021 systematic review of clinical studies assessed skin health outcomes [4], and a 2018 comprehensive review summarised its role in skin repair and disease [6].

UV-induced deterioration: a 10-week double-blind trial in 23 healthy Japanese participants evaluated dietary astaxanthin on UV-induced skin deterioration [5]. The trial was small and enrolled healthy Japanese participants, which limits how far results generalise.

Other conditions: an evidence-based review focused on human clinical trials covers a wide range of therapeutic uses [7]. Randomized trials have examined digital eye strain in children [8], endometriosis patients undergoing assisted reproduction [9], PCOS [10] and oxidative stress [11]. A registered study examined astaxanthin in Alzheimer disease [15] and pharmacokinetics of yeast-derived astaxanthin [14].
Supplements are generally well tolerated at studied doses; reviews of human trials describe them as generally well tolerated [7]. Safety in pregnancy and long-term use is not well established.

Astaxanthin is a lipid-soluble, amphiphilic carotenoid with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity; a review reported the highest oxygen radical absorbance capacity among related carotenoids in vitro [1][12]. Dietary algal astaxanthin is esterified, and evidence supports de-esterification in the intestine before absorption [1].

It is a metabolite of zeaxanthin and canthaxanthin containing both hydroxyl and ketone groups, with three stereoisomers; synthetic astaxanthin contains a mixture of all three in roughly 1:2:1 proportions. Its structure was described by synthesis in 1975 [1].

sections.h: Use in looksmaxxing and fitness communities
paras: T Nation threads from 2008 to 2013 mention astaxanthin as an anti-inflammatory supplement, as a possible way to control oestrogen in TRT users, and as part of daily supplement stacks at doses of a few milligrams [17][18][19][20].

lore.intro: On T Nation, astaxanthin is mentioned as an anti-inflammatory and general-health supplement; appearance-specific use is mainly reported in skincare circles [16][19][18].

claims.believers: Posters describe it and green-lipped mussel oil as extremely potent anti-inflammatories for athletes [19].
claims.experts: Reviews describe antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activity in vitro and in small trials; evidence for clinical benefit varies by condition [12][7].

claims.claim: It improves skin moisture and elasticity
claims.believers: The authors of a 2018 review describe mounting evidence of nutraceutical applications in dermatology [6].
claims.experts: A 2021 meta-analysis found significant improvements in moisture and elasticity but not wrinkle depth [3].

claims.claim: It protects against UV skin damage
claims.believers: A 2018 trial evaluated it as a dietary protector against UV-induced skin deterioration [5].
claims.experts: A 23-person trial evaluated UV-induced skin deterioration; reviews describe the evidence as limited and the trials small [5][4].

claims.claim: It helps control oestrogen on TRT
claims.believers: One T Nation poster recommended it as a natural option for controlling E2 [20].
claims.experts: No published trials reviewed here have tested astaxanthin for oestrogen control in men on testosterone therapy.
